skill.name: quality-manager-qmr
skill.description: Senior Quality Manager Responsible Person (QMR) for HealthTech and MedTech companies. Provides overall quality system responsibility, regulatory compliance oversight, management accountability, and strategic quality leadership. Use for quality system governance, regulatory compliance oversight, management responsibility, and quality strategic planning.
skill.summary: Guide QMR governance, regulatory oversight, management review, and quality strategy for HealthTech and MedTech organizations.

content.value_statement: HealthTech teams must coordinate quality governance, regulatory oversight, and management review across complex obligations. This skill provides structured QMR frameworks for planning, monitoring, escalation, and executive reporting.
actual_capabilities: Structures QMR responsibilities across quality oversight, compliance, management accountability, and continuous improvement.
Guides compliance reviews for EU MDR, FDA QSR, ISO 13485, and national requirements.
Organizes management review topics, quality dashboards, strategic planning, and executive reporting.
Integrates quality responsibilities across research, manufacturing, supply chain, and commercial teams.
Defines quality KPIs, cost categories, audit oversight, certification activities, and escalation points.
limitations: Does not replace qualified legal, regulatory, clinical, or certification advice.
Does not verify current requirements for a specific product, market, or jurisdiction.
Named QMR scripts, references, templates, and dashboards are not included as implemented resources.
Does not connect to live quality systems, regulatory databases, or company records.

use_cases.title: Prepare Management Review
use_cases.description: Build an agenda covering QMS performance, compliance status, customer feedback, quality costs, resources, decisions, and follow-up.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Market Compliance
use_cases.description: Map oversight priorities across ISO 13485, EU MDR, FDA QSR, and applicable national requirements.

use_cases.title: Set Quality Strategy
use_cases.description: Align quality objectives, investments, KPIs, culture initiatives, and cross-functional responsibilities with business goals.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Responsibility Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a QMR responsibility matrix for [company type], covering QMS oversight, regulatory compliance, management reporting, and continuous improvement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a clear overview of QMR ownership.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Management Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a quarterly management review agenda for [company], using these metrics: [metrics]. Include decisions, owners, escalation criteria, and required follow-up.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a structured executive quality meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Compliance Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this QMS summary against ISO 13485, EU MDR, and FDA expectations: [summary]. Identify gaps, priorities, evidence needs, and management actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare existing practices with multiple regulatory frameworks.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Quality Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a three-year quality strategy for [company and markets]. Integrate regulatory risk, resources, KPIs, quality costs, culture, audits, and executive governance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create an advanced, cross-functional quality roadmap.

output_examples.input: Build a quarterly management review agenda for a Class II medical device company.
output: QMS performance: audits, nonconformities, corrective actions, complaints, and process trends.
Regulatory status: FDA obligations, ISO 13485 certification, emerging requirements, and inspection readiness.
Decisions: resource priorities, risk escalations, improvement owners, deadlines, and effectiveness checks.

output_examples.input: Propose quality priorities for a HealthTech company entering the European Union.
output: Confirm product classification, conformity pathway, and QMS scope.
Assign ownership for technical documentation, post-market activities, supplier controls, and regulatory monitoring.
Track readiness through evidence-based milestones, executive reviews, and documented risk escalation.

output_examples.input: Define a concise quality cost dashboard.
output: Prevention costs: planning, training, supplier development, and risk controls.
Appraisal costs: inspection, testing, audits, and certification.
Failure costs: rework, scrap, returns, complaints, recalls, and regulatory actions.

best_practices: Provide company size, product type, target markets, current certifications, and known quality risks.
Validate every recommendation against controlled procedures and current jurisdiction-specific requirements.
Assign owners, due dates, evidence, escalation thresholds, and effectiveness measures to each action.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated guidance as regulatory approval or legal advice.
Do not create universal controls without considering product risk, market requirements, and organizational maturity.
Do not report performance without source data, definitions, owners, and review periods.

faq.question: What does this skill help a QMR produce?
faq.answer: It helps structure responsibility matrices, management reviews, compliance assessments, quality strategies, KPI frameworks, and executive reports.

faq.question: Which regulatory frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance references ISO 13485, EU MDR 2017/745, FDA QSR 21 CFR 820, and national requirements.

faq.question: Can it confirm regulatory compliance?
faq.answer: No. Qualified personnel must verify compliance using current laws, standards, product evidence, and controlled procedures.

faq.question: Does it include working dashboards or automation?
faq.answer: No. The package contains placeholder support files, while the named QMR dashboards and automation resources are not implemented.

faq.question: What information improves the output?
faq.answer: Provide product classification, markets, QMS scope, certifications, audit results, quality metrics, risks, resources, and deadlines.

faq.question: Can executives use this skill directly?
faq.answer: Yes. Executives can use it to frame governance decisions, resource priorities, quality objectives, escalation paths, and management review questions.
